test_title: Most Repeated 2025 Current Affairs PYQ Subject Test - 01
subject: general
question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals — National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, published in June 2025, what percentage of the rural population used improved sources of drinking water during the year 2024–2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**99.62%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals — National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025**, was released in **June 2025** by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• According to the report, during the assessment year **2024–2025**, the percentage of the **rural population** using improved sources of drinking water reached **99.62%**. ***Hence, the correct option is 99.62%.***
 
• This indicator is a vital metric under **SDG Goal 6**, which specifically targets **Clean Water and Sanitation** for all citizens.
 
• The data indicates a significant upward trajectory in rural infrastructure development, ensuring that nearly the entire rural landscape has access to safe and improved water sources.
 
• The report serves as a monitoring tool for the **United Nations' 2030 Agenda**, tracking India's specific progress through the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**, which currently consists of over **300 indicators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation):** 
 
 
• This goal aims to ensure the **availability and sustainable management of water** and sanitation for all by the year **2030**.
 
• India's commitment to this goal is reflected in large-scale schemes designed to eliminate the disparity between **urban** and **rural** access.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM):** 
 
 
• Launched on **15th August 2019**, this mission is a primary driver for the high percentage recorded in the 2025 report.
 
• The mission aims to provide **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural household, often referred to as **"Har Ghar Jal,"** by **2024-25**.
 
• It emphasizes **community-based management** and greywater treatment to ensure long-term sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Improved Sources of Drinking Water:** 
 
 
• This category includes **piped water** into dwellings, **public taps** or standpipes, **tube wells** or boreholes, protected dug wells, and **rainwater harvesting** systems.
 
• The use of improved sources is critical in reducing **water-borne diseases** such as cholera, dysentery, and typhoid in **rural India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):** 
 
 
• **MoSPI** is the nodal agency in India responsible for the development of the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**.
 
• It coordinates with various **Central Ministries** and **State Governments** to collect authenticated data for the **SDG Progress Reports**.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework (NIF):** 
 
 
• The **NIF** is the backbone of **SDG monitoring** in India, localized to suit the Indian context while remaining aligned with **Global Indicators**.
 
• The **2025 Progress Report** highlights that India has made "substantial progress" in **Goal 6**, with the rural drinking water target being one of the most successful outcomes.
 
• Data for this specific indicator is often sourced from the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
 
 

e5
